Manageable

/MAN-ij-uh-bul/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Manageable means able to be handled, controlled, or accomplished without excessive difficulty.

Splitting the massive report into weekly sections finally made the workload manageable.

Worked Example

A first-year teacher stared at a stack of 120 end-of-term essays and nearly panicked. Then she built a plan: fifteen essays a night, a strict rubric, and a timer to keep each one under eight minutes. The stack that had looked impossible on Monday became manageable by Tuesday evening, and she returned every essay, graded and annotated, by Friday. The work never got smaller; it simply stopped being overwhelming.

Once the grading was broken into controlled pieces, it could be handled without being overwhelming, which is exactly what manageable means.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

doable: Doable means able to be done or carried out — a quick, informal thumbs-up that the thing can happen at all. Manageable says more about the experience of doing it: the size or difficulty can be handled without overwhelming you. A marathon is doable for many runners; a training plan is what makes the miles manageable.

controllable: Controllable means able to be kept under control, and it fits forces and behavior — a controllable burn, a controllable skid. Manageable is about workload and difficulty: a task or amount you can cope with without being swamped. You control what might run away from you; you manage what might pile up on you.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

overwhelming: too great or intense to handle

unwieldy: hard to handle because of its size or complexity

Where it sits · how much struggle it takes — survivable → manageable → effortless

survivable vs. manageable: Survivable means you can barely get through something, while manageable means you can handle it without being overwhelmed.

effortless vs. manageable: Manageable still takes real effort and attention, but an effortless task practically does itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — manage

Root — manage: from Italian maneggiare, to handle or train a horse, from Latin manus, hand

Suffix — -able

Suffix — -able: able to be

Put it together

Put it together: Manageable is built on manage, from Italian maneggiare, 'to handle or train a horse,' which traces back to Latin manus, 'hand.' Something manageable is literally something you can get your hands around, and the spelling keeps the e of manage so the g stays soft.

Use the root in a new word: manual

Use the root in a new word: manual: A manual transmission is shifted by hand, exactly what the Latin root manus promises.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral, everyday-to-professional register

Manageable speaks only to difficulty, saying a task, size, or amount can be handled without overwhelming you (a manageable workload, manageable debt). It makes no promise of benefit: a manageable problem is still a problem, just one you can cope with.
